36.1: Decode a five-byte educational SPI packet. Fields: mode, expected_mode, elapsed_us, timeout_us, expected_seq, frame. Modes 0..3, bytes 0..255. Packet [0xA5, seq, signed16_hi, signed16_lo, XOR of preceding bytes]. Deadline equality succeeds. The simulator knows endpoint mode metadata; real SPI mode faults are not always self-identifying.
36.2: Simulate integer-tick, single-core, preemptive fixed-priority periodic tasks. Each task has name, period, cost, deadline and priority (lower wins). All first releases occur at tick 0. horizon is 1..10000; deadlines are relative and <= period. Deadline misses count unfinished jobs when their deadline occurs, not merely at horizon.
36.3: Lint a deliberately small board-review record, not a KiCad file. Required fields: supply_v, min_v, max_v, load_ma, budget_ma, footprint_verified and return_path_continuous. Report sorted issues. Even an empty list means only ready for qualified review, never authorization to fabricate or power hardware.
36.4: Choose the first diagnostic action from Boolean observations: over_limit, power_ok, reset_released, clock_ok, id_ok, framing_ok. Check safety first, then power, reset, clock, identity and framing. This is a simulated decision tree, not a device-specific physical procedure.
37.1: Compute active-lane efficiency in an educational serialized-path group. paths is a nonempty list of A/B values of length <= width. Path costs and common cost are integer issue slots; at least one slot must execute. Count inactive tail lanes in capacity. This is not a cycle-accurate GPU model or an occupancy calculator.
37.2: Count unique byte-addressed sectors touched by one modeled memory instruction, including cross-sector words and repeated addresses. Fields: addresses, word_bytes (1..128), sector_bytes (1..4096). useful_unique_bytes is not the logical byte count for broadcast reads. Cache reuse, merging across instructions and actual DRAM traffic are not simulated.
37.3: Compute a resource-service lower bound with ideal overlap and a serial service estimate. demands and rates are dictionaries with identical nonempty resource keys; setup_s is nonnegative. All rates must be positive. Neither result is a hardware timing guarantee: queuing and dependencies are omitted.
37.4: Model one serialized request with setup, upload, compute, readback and synchronization. input_bytes/output_bytes count payload; bandwidth_Bps is effective payload bytes/second. For shared=True, use visibility_s instead of explicit copies. compute_s already includes kernel memory service. Only explicit transfer phases are removed; ownership and visibility costs remain.
38.1: Return an Amdahl speedup and roofline bound. Inputs: unchanged_fraction in [0,1], acceleration >0, added_fraction >=0, compute_GFLOPs >0, bandwidth_GBs >0, intensity_FLOP_per_byte >=0. Added overhead is expressed as a fraction of ORIGINAL runtime. Decimal GB and GFLOP units cancel.
38.2: Summarize raw times only after every output checksum passes. Fields: times_ns, checksums, expected_checksum, warmup (number of leading samples excluded). Positive finite times required; all samples, including warmup, must validate. Report retained n, mean, median and nearest-rank p95; no post-hoc outlier removal.
38.3: Model job placement. costs are nonnegative service times, workers is 1..256, overhead is per-job service cost. policy is round_robin or greedy (earliest available worker, ties lowest index). All jobs are ready at t=0. This does not simulate NUMA, work stealing, real threads or vector instructions.
38.4: Integrate interval-average power. times_s has one more item than power_w and completed_frames, and is strictly increasing. Each power value describes the entire following interval, not an instantaneous sample. Return energy, duration, average power and completed frames per joule; zero energy yields null efficiency.
39.1: Summarize a synthetic one-clock input/presentation trace. input_ms and present_ms are same-length lists with at least two rows; presentation is strictly increasing and never precedes its corresponding input. timestamp_kind must equal synthetic_present. Return mean/p95 input-to-modeled-present and presentation-interval extrema. No photon measurement is inferred.
39.2: Simulate persistent progress independently of volatile graphics resources. Start RUNNING at tick 0, resource generation 1. Events: step, checkpoint, suspend, resume, kill, launch. suspend checkpoints in this educational contract; sudden kill does not. kill discards uncheckpointed progress. Resuming rebuilds resources with a new generation. Unsupported transitions raise ValueError.
39.3: Compute an educational stereo pose in meters with +Y up and -Z forward. Head yaw is right-handed about +Y. Constant linear velocity predicts head translation between sample_s and target_s (0..0.1 seconds ahead). Eye offsets +/-ipd_m/2 are rotated into world coordinates. tracking_valid=False returns no invented pose. This is not an OpenXR runtime implementation.
39.4: Negotiate required and optional capabilities without guessing vendor access. supported, required and optional are lists of strings. Return sorted missing requirements and enabled optional capabilities. A backend is accepted only if every required capability is advertised. This structural check does not certify a platform.
40.1: Calculate a bounded additive-frame proposal. frame_ms >0; 0<= operation_ms <= frame_ms; acceleration >0; overhead_ms >=0. maximum_saved_fraction assumes the operation disappears with zero overhead. New frame time uses the supplied finite acceleration. An overlapped operation off the critical path cannot use this model without justification.
40.2: Apply a signed fixed-point affine transform with explicit rounding and saturation. x and gain are signed encoded integers with bits (2..32) and frac (0..bits-1) fractional bits. Compute nearest-even(x*gain / 2**frac) + bias, then saturate to bits. bias is an encoded signed integer in the same format. Return raw integer outputs; Python arbitrary-precision intermediates avoid overflow.
40.3: Simulate one registered 4-byte-word buffer with explicit ownership. capacity is bytes. Events submit(offset,count), timeout, complete(epoch), reset. Submission validates alignment and subtraction-based bounds; zero count is rejected. A timeout quarantines the buffer and completion cannot release a quarantined buffer. reset models acknowledged device quiescence, advances epoch, and reclaims the buffer. No actual DMA occurs.
40.4: Check evidence-ledger structure. Each claim needs id, tier, artifact, requirement, limitations; known_artifacts is a list of paths. Allowed tiers: analytical, functional_model, cycle_model, synthesis, host_measurement, physical_measurement. Report structural omissions, not scientific approval. Arbitrary unsupported tiers never become measurements by renaming files.
